title: Derived scalar transitivity preserves the specified projective-line Kummer morphism
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $N\geq1$ be invertible on $S$, and let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings with $NA=NB=0$. Put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/N$, $P=\mathbf P^1_S$, and let $\mathcal O_P(1)$ have transition $g_0=(x_1/x_0)^{-1}g_1$ on the standard affine charts. Use the ordinary etale derived categories of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $R=\Lambda,A,B$ put $R_P(1)=\mu_{N,P}\otimes_{\Lambda_P}R_P$, with the roots-of-unity sheaf and its power action as in [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], and let $E_{\Lambda R}=-\otimes^L_{\Lambda_P}R_P$ and $E=-\otimes^L_{A_P}B_P$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

Let $c_\Lambda:\Lambda_P\to\mu_{N,P}[2]$ be the Kummer first Chern morphism of the fixed $\mathcal O_P(1)$: the Kummer connecting class of its line-bundle class, in the module-derived interpretation used by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction]. Let $c_R:R_P\to R_P(1)[2]$ for $R=A,B$ be the image $E_{\Lambda R}(c_\Lambda)$ under the canonical unit and degree-zero Tate identifications; thus its adjunct for $q:P\to S$ is the specified Kummer component $h_R$ of that node.

Let $\alpha:E E_{\Lambda A}\xrightarrow\sim E_{\Lambda B}$ be the canonical composition comparison of derived coefficient extension [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Its components on $\Lambda_P$ and $\mu_{N,P}[2]$, under the preceding identifications, are respectively the multiplication map $\theta^0:E(A_P)\xrightarrow\sim B_P$ and the shifted balanced map $\theta^1[2]:E(A_P(1)[2])\xrightarrow\sim B_P(1)[2]$ induced by $(z\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto z\otimes\varphi(a)b$. With the canonical shift comparison understood,
$$\theta^1[2]\circ E(c_A)=c_B\circ\theta^0.$$
This is an equality in the derived category, for arbitrary $\varphi$; no flatness of either coefficient extension is assumed.

proof.text: Apply normalized endpoint existence to the residue-to-A, composite residue-to-B and A-to-B maps on P. Apply the scalar Chern theorem to the same fixed residue arrow and each residue endpoint.
Apply endpoint composition to obtain the unit and shifted Tate-line equations for the specified canonical composition comparison.

Apply naturality of the canonical composition isomorphism to the fixed residue Chern arrow. Precompose by extension of the unit endpoint isomorphism, expand chernImage, substitute the two component equations and cancel all inverse pairs. This gives the last derived equality.
